newsitem.title: UK: UK govt says Britain's position on EMU clear.
newsitem.headline: UK govt says Britain's position on EMU clear.

text.p: The government's position on whether or not Britain would enter a single European currency remains clear and unchanged, an aide from Prime Minister John Major's office said on Wednesday.

The aide also said he expected a Treasury report, on whether or not other countries were fudging the economic criteria for entry, would not be ready until next year. He said he was unaware of any other Treasury report for discussion at the cabinet.
The Financial Times reported on Wednesday that the cabinet would back Prime Minister John Major's wait-and-see policy on a single currency at its meeting on Thursday.

The cabinet backing, which would put an end to argument about whether the government will harden its policy before the election, would be given on the basis of a briefing paper issued by the Treasury, the newspaper said.

It said the briefing paper came to the conclusion there was no way a judgement could be made on whether countries were joining a single currency on the basis of "fudged" criteria until at least nine months after the election.

An unnamed minister was quoted by the newspaper as saying the briefing paper "completely underpins everything that the Prime Minister and the Chancellor have been saying, that there will be no opportunity to take a firm view on whether or not to join a single currency until after the general election."
Major, lagging in polls and dogged by party splits over Europe, must call an election by May.
